title: Delivery & Pickup Appointments: Accepted Refusal Findings and Transport Damage Limits
content:
For Delivery & Pickup Appointments, the claims desk works to the following findings and limits for each fulfillment method. They cover the condition-report findings that let a buyer refuse the vehicle at handover as vehicle unavailable, the period after handover in which new damage must be reported to count as transport damage, and the most Kestrel pays to repair it.

## Accepted refusal findings

All six fulfillment methods accept the same three condition-report findings as grounds for refusal:

- Odometer variance
- New cosmetic damage
- New mechanical issue

Each method lists exactly these three findings, with no additions and no omissions.

## Transport damage limits

| Fulfillment method | Hours after handover within which new damage must be reported to be treated as transport damage | Most Kestrel pays to repair reported transport damage |
|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Hub Pickup | 24 hours | $500.00 |
| Kestrel Vending Tower Pickup | 24 hours | $500.00 |
| Kestrel Fly & Drive | 24 hours | $500.00 |
| Kestrel Local Home Delivery | 48 hours | $750.00 |
| Kestrel Extended-Zone Delivery | 48 hours | $1000.00 |
| Kestrel Enclosed White-Glove Delivery | 72 hours | $2500.00 |

## Reading the limits (hypothetical reports)

- If a Local Home Delivery buyer reports new damage 30 hours after handover, the report is within that method's 48 hours. The same 30-hour report on a Hub Pickup falls outside its 24 hours, so the damage is not treated as transport damage.
- The repair limit grows with the method: $500.00 for the three pickup methods, $750.00 for Local Home Delivery, $1000.00 for Extended-Zone Delivery and $2500.00 for Enclosed White-Glove Delivery.
